progressive dyspnea, lethargy, and recumbency
temperature was 38.5 °C
heart rate, 170 beats/min with regular rhythm
respiratory rate, 60 breaths/min
jugular pulses were present and mucous membranes were cyanotic
a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle

concepts.why: The presence of a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice suggest Tricuspid Atresia.
The presence of a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects suggest Ventricular Septal Defect.
The presence of cyanotic mucous membranes, a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur, and severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle suggest Tetralogy of Fallot.
The presence of cyanotic mucous membranes and severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle suggest Pulmonary Atresia.
The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle and a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle suggest Double Outlet Right Ventricle.
The presence of a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur and severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle suggest Ebstein's Anomaly.
The presence of severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects suggest Tricuspid Regurgitation.
The presence of severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle and a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle suggest Right Ventricular Hypoplasia.
